key_insight: A single high-resolution turbulent realization contains enough recurring multiscale structure to train a patch-based super-resolution model that reconstructs unseen flow fields with high fidelity.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-efficient path for recovering fine-scale turbulence features when high-resolution simulation or measurement data are scarce.
method: Train a WDSR network only on overlapping patches from one high-resolution 2D homogeneous isotropic turbulence snapshot.
Predict super-resolved patches for unseen fields and stitch them with Hann-window-weighted overlap-add.
Benchmark against interpolation and WDSR models trained on 1, 25, 50, and 100 full snapshots.
evidence_signal: At x32 and x64 super-resolution, the method recovers coherent vortices and improves high-wavenumber energy and multiscale statistics relative to conventional interpolation.
watch_item: Performance may depend on spatial stationarity and patch overlap quality, so results may not transfer directly to non-homogeneous or transient flows without retraining.
paper_title: Extreme-Scale Super-Resolution of Homogeneous Turbulence from a Single Realization
